Test the midpoint temperature between injections 9 and 10, which had different critical pairs. This may balance their selectivity shifts and resolve both bottlenecks while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Keep the gradient fixed and test a larger temperature shift to move beyond the selectivity crossings seen at 30–40 C. The hotter run should shorten retention and may separate the troublesome central cluster in a different elution order.

Retain injection 15 as the maximum-score benchmark and test a lower starting organic fraction with a steeper gradient. Stronger initial retention may improve the early cluster enough to permit faster elution without losing full resolution.
